bib.title: Generating Wikipedia by Summarizing Long Sequences

question: Can English Wikipedia lead sections be generated as multi-document summarization of reference documents, and can a decoder-only model handle the very long inputs?
hypothesis: A decoder-only Transformer with local and memory-compressed attention handles longer inputs than encoder-decoder models and performs better on long sequences.
contributions: WikiSum: Wikipedia lead generation as a large multi-document summarization dataset
Transformer decoder (T-D) and T-DMCA with local and memory-compressed attention for long sequences
Preliminary generation of entire Wikipedia articles

method.summary: Stage 1 ranks paragraphs of cited and web-search documents (tf-idf against the title) and keeps the first L tokens. Stage 2 trains an abstractive model (seq2seq-att, Transformer enc-dec, decoder-only T-D, or T-DMCA) to write the Wikipedia lead.

datasets.name: WikiSum
datasets.split: roughly 80/10/10; only articles with at least one crawlable citation
datasets.source: Wikipedia articles, text of crawlable cited documents, and top 10 Google results per section-title query (Wikipedia page and clones removed)
datasets.preprocessing: clone detected if max unigram recall over article sections r>0.5; paragraphs ranked, concatenated with title prefix, sub-word tokenised, truncated to L tokens; output not truncated

models.name: Transformer encoder-decoder (T-ED)
models.context: best L=500-1000; unable to learn at L=2000

models.name: Transformer decoder (T-D)
models.params: almost half of T-ED for the same hyper-parameter set
models.architecture: decoder part of T-ED; input, separator and output as one sequence, plain LM

models.name: Transformer decoder with memory-compressed attention (T-DMCA)
models.architecture: 5 layers LMLML alternating local attention (blocks of 256 tokens) and memory-compressed attention (strided conv kernel 3 stride 3 on keys/values); optional MoE layer (128 or 256 experts)

training.objective: maximum likelihood; T-D/T-DMCA next-token over input and output
training.steps: 1 million steps (T-ED); not stated for others
training.regularisation: none; little overfitting, no early stopping

other.full_article_models: T-DMCA with L=6000 reference tokens predicting at most 2192 article tokens; title-only model up to 4000 tokens

inference.decoding: beam search size 4, length penalty alpha=0.6, decode until end-of-sequence
inference.prompting: input sequence given first, output generated autoregressively after separator
inference.retrieval: tf-idf paragraph ranking against the article title; first L tokens kept

metrics.name: per-wordpiece (log-)perplexity
metrics.definition: per-wordpiece perplexity on test set; tables print log-perplexity values

metrics.name: ROUGE-L F1
metrics.definition: ROUGE-1.5.5, harmonic mean of recall and precision

metrics.name: DUC-style linguistic quality
metrics.definition: 1-5 scores on 5 dimensions; 25 examples per model, 3 raters of 7

eval.protocol: Welch two sample t-test p=0.001 for human scores; side-by-side 3 raters x 25 examples; single runs

limits: Full-article generation is preliminary and not tuned
Comparison with Sauper & Barzilay is best-effort: lead vs article, different subsets, clone detection unknown
Extractive stage is a coarse bottleneck; authors suggest supervised relevance
Optimizer, learning rate, batch size and steps for T-D/T-DMCA unstated; single runs
Side-by-side human evaluation gets harder at the high end
Models translate names across languages, not systematically evaluated
